title: Test site · Titanic tile
memorial_note: Fixture text for automated tests. The real Titanic site is a grave: more than 1,500 people died in the sinking on 15 April 1912.

entries.title: About this test site
paragraphs: This landmark folder is a test fixture. It reuses the Titanic tile's real GMRT bathymetry so the scan, discovery and field-guide systems can be exercised without the authored Titanic content.
It is referenced by no scan target, so it is unlocked from the start.

sources.title: Ryan et al. (2009), Global Multi-Resolution Topography synthesis

entries.title: The bow section
paragraphs: The forward part of the hull came to rest upright on the abyssal plain, about 3,800 m down, after the ship broke apart during the sinking.
The wreck was located on 1 September 1985 by a joint French-American expedition. The stern section lies roughly 600 m away.
What you see here is a placed model at the recorded position, not survey data: the bathymetry grid is far too coarse to resolve a 269 m hull.
